rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use blanket bans against applicants with arrests or convictions; they must consider criminal history case-by-case, excluding arrests without conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, and convictions older than 5 years (with limited safety exceptions). Providers also may not use an applicant's credit score alone to approve or deny housing.
rules.key_value: 5-year conviction lookback limit; no blanket criminal bans; no credit-score-based denial
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or that have income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where a direct relationship exists between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of harm to others; does not apply to current criminal behavior; federal or state law requirements preempt the policy where conflicting.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the housing provider receives DND funding/land or has BPDA inclusionary income-restricted units

rules.conflict_note: This is a city policy document (not an ordinance) applicable only to subsidized/income-restricted or DND-funded housing providers, not to general market-rate multifamily buildings; federal/state law preempts where conflicting.
